title: Vesper and the Hollow
premise: Ines Ashgrove, a cartographer who maps realms that shouldn't exist, has spent years keeping his head down in the Guild of Impossible Things, trading in wonders he never touches. When a dying courier presses a soul-map into his hands—a chart of a soul sold to the Hollow Court beneath Mount Vesper—he becomes hunted by both the guild's masters and the court's collectors. With a found family of outcasts, Ines descends through thirteen turning moons to steal back the stranger's soul, discovering it is bound to his own forgotten past. He succeeds only by surrendering his own name to the ledger, choosing connection over invisibility, and returns changed: visible, known, and finally free.
about_author: Bram Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about people who trade in the impossible and pay for it in ordinary ways.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Wonders
chapters.summary: Ines Ashgrove catalogs an impossible compass for the Guild, revealing his careful, invisible life among traders of marvels. His POV establishes his rule: map everything, touch nothing. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A bleeding courier collapses in the guild's alley, pressing a folded map into Ines's hands and whispering 'thirteen turns' before dying. The map shows a soul—his own signature on the sale contract. Emotional beat: terror breaking routine.

chapters.title: What the Guild Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines hides the map but guildmaster Corvane Dusk notices the courier's death. Ines lies for the first time in years. POV alternates briefly to Corvane, who suspects. Emotional beat: the first crack in Ines's armor of anonymity.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Sings
chapters.summary: Ines seeks help from Wren, a guild thief who once owed him a favor. She recognizes the map as Hollow Court work. Her POV reveals she lost a brother to the mountain. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, first spark of found family.

chapters.title: Collectors at Moonrise
chapters.summary: Hollow Court collectors raid the guild quarter hunting the map. Ines and Wren escape through a mapped-then-unmapped alley only Ines can navigate. His POV. Emotional beat: his cartography saves lives—power he never claimed.

chapters.title: The Ninth Turn
chapters.summary: They recruit Oskar, a disgraced moon-priest who can read the lunar countdown; four turns remain. Oskar's POV exposes the court's bargain: souls fuel the mountain's immortality. Emotional beat: dread mixed with purpose.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane offers Ines protection in exchange for the map, revealing the guild has sold souls before—including, perhaps, Ines's own memories. Ines refuses. His POV. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that raised him.

chapters.title: Road Beneath the World
chapters.summary: The trio flees into the Underways using Ines's hand-drawn charts. Wren's POV: campfire scene where they share losses, becoming something like family. Emotional beat: warmth earned through vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: They pass through a bazaar where identities are currency. Ines nearly sells his name to buy passage but Wren stops him. His POV. Emotional beat: temptation of erasure versus the pull of being known.

chapters.title: Echoes in the Deep
chapters.summary: Oskar's POV. The Underways echo with sold souls; one calls Ines by a childhood name. Flashback fragments suggest Ines's past is entangled with the court. Emotional beat: vertigo of a self unraveling.

chapters.title: The Gate of Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: They reach the mountain gate as the twelfth turn begins. A collector offers Ines his old life back if he abandons the quest. His POV. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Inside Mount Vesper: a court of pale nobles feasting on memory. Ines maps their halls in secret, finding the soul-vault. Tense stealth sequence. Emotional beat: courage sharpened by fear.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The trio infiltrates a masque; Wren dances with the Hollow Queen to buy time. The Queen names Ines aloud—the name he forgot. Emotional beat: recognition as both wound and key.

chapters.title: The Sold Boy
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, heavy flashback: he was a child sold to the court, whose soul escaped incomplete; the dying courier carried the missing half. The map leads home to himself. Emotional beat: devastating self-reckoning.

chapters.title: Corvane's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Corvane arrives to trade the trio to the Queen for guild privileges. Oskar is captured covering their escape. His sacrifice shown in his final POV. Emotional beat: grief and fury fusing the found family tighter.

chapters.title: The Vault of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Ines and Wren breach the soul-vault, where stolen selves sit in jars like preserved fruit. Ines finds the courier's soul—and the shard bearing his own name. His POV. Emotional beat: awe curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: The moon completes its turn; the vault seals. Trapped, Ines chooses to rewrite the map itself, redrawing the vault's boundaries with his blood and craft. His POV. Emotional beat: the cartographer finally touching what he maps.

chapters.title: The Queen's Bargain
chapters.summary: The Hollow Queen corners them: she'll free the souls if someone takes her place as the mountain's anchor. Wren volunteers; Ines refuses to let her. Climax begins. Emotional beat: love against sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Ines Ashgrove Gave
chapters.summary: Climax. Ines offers not his life but his name—writing himself out of every ledger, including the court's, unbinding all contracts. The Queen's power collapses without written claim. Emotional beat: triumph through surrender.

chapters.title: Collapse of the Hollow
chapters.summary: The mountain exhales its stolen souls; freed shades carry Oskar's body toward dawn. Ines, nameless, cannot remember why he is crying. Wren holds his hand anyway. Emotional beat: catharsis amid loss.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Resolution. Above ground, Wren speaks a new name for him—not taken, but given. The guild, gutted by scandal, reforms under survivors. Ines begins mapping a world where nothing is sold. Emotional beat: tentative hope.

chapters.title: Vesper and the Hollow
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ines's POV. Years later, a child brings him a strange map, echoing the story's beginning—but this time Ines opens the door willingly, family around him. Emotional beat: full-circle peace; invisibility traded for belonging.
